goal: Let the user watch the agent's state while a page waits on it
how: One span with data-orb naming what the agent is doing, and an aria-label in the reader's words; changing the attribute changes the drawing. waiting, error and done take warn, danger and go, so the states the reader acts on are not read as work still running.
avoid: Naming the orb after its attribute, "waiting", rather than what the reader would want to hear, "Waiting for your approval".

goal: Let the user see what an agent is busy with right now
how: An .agent-status pill holding an orb and a label that says what the agent is doing, with the time once the wait is worth counting and a stop button last for long work. .text-shimmer on the label while it works; --warn when it waits on the reader.
avoid: A label that says only "Working…", which does not tell the reader whether to wait.

goal: Let the user see which element of the page the agent is changing
phrases: highlight what the ai is editing
how: .beam draws an edge in the agent's colours on the element's own border — a card, a field, the composer — so it needs no wrapper and keeps the focus ring; remove the class when the work is done.
avoid: Leaving the beam on after the work ends, which tells the reader the agent still holds that part of the page.

goal: Let the user see that an answer is still being written
how: .chat-bubble--streaming puts a caret after the last block while text arrives, with the bubble aria-busy until the answer is whole and a status pill under it saying what the agent is doing. Before the first words, .skeleton--agent holds the answer's shape.
avoid: Leaving the bubble announced while it streams, so a screen reader reads every word as it lands.

goal: Let the user tell what an agent generated from what a person wrote
how: A .badge-ai beside the generated content, in the card head or the list row, with the word written out; the sparkle is decoration.
avoid: The sparkle icon alone, which says nothing to a screen reader and little to anyone else.

goal: Let the user see how sure the agent is of its answer
how: .confidence with data-level 1, 2 or 3 fills that many bars in warn, info or go beside words that say the level; a low score says what to do about it.
avoid: Letting the bars carry the level: they are aria-hidden, and the words are what is read.

goal: Let the user see how much of the agent's context window is used
how: A .context-ring filled to --value, a role="meter" with the value in aria-valuenow, --warn and --danger as it fills. In a ghost button it opens a hover card that breaks the window down by kind of token, with what each cost.
avoid: A ring with no number anywhere, which tells the reader that it is filling but not how near the limit it is.

goal: Let the user tell which agent is which
how: An .agent-avatar wherever a person's avatar would go, in a tone the agent keeps for good, with its name written beside it. Its state moves the sphere but never changes its colour.
avoid: Changing an agent's tone to show its state: the tone is how a reader tells two agents apart in a long thread.

goal: Let the user meet the agent as a character whose moods follow its work
how: <SednaMochi /> once in the host page, then a .mochi span per appearance whose data-action and data-mood are set as the work moves on; the joints ease from pose to pose. .mochi--still keeps it calm for a reader who wants it so.
avoid: Letting Mochi carry the news: the words say what happened, and Mochi says how it feels.

goal: Let the user see the agent sitting on a card or pointing at a control
how: The Mochi and the element share a .mochi-host and data-perch says which edge it sits on, peeks over or hangs from; point stands it beside an anchor named with anchor-name, with no script.
avoid: Forgetting the room a perch needs: it draws outside the element, and the host does not grow for it.

goal: Let the user read how the agent reached its answer
how: A details.reasoning folded under a summary that says how long the agent thought; while it thinks, data-state="running" shimmers the label beside a stop button, and the words change to what it took once it is done.
avoid: Showing the reasoning open by default, which buries the answer most readers came for.

goal: Let the user check the steps and tools an agent ran and what came back
how: Each call a details card with the tool's name, a status badge in the app's words and the time, opening on what it was sent and what came back as code blocks. A failed call and one waiting for approval are written open.
avoid: Describing a call in words instead of showing it: the code block is what lets the reader check the agent's work.

goal: Let the user approve or deny what an agent wants to do
how: An .agent-approval card names the change from and to, chips say what kind of change it is, and the foot offers Approve as go solid, Take over as warn and Deny quietly. Once answered, data-state swaps the actions for who answered and when, with an undo while it can still be taken back.
avoid: Approve and deny as Yes and No: each button says what it does, and approve takes go because it lets the action out.

goal: Let the user answer a question the agent asks in the middle of a task
how: .agent-approval--question in the info colours, each question a fieldset with its legend — choice tiles for one answer, checkboxes for several, a labelled field for free text — and Send disabled until every required question has an answer.
avoid: A free-text field for a question with a few known answers, which choice tiles answer in one press.

goal: Let the user follow the agent's plan and what is queued behind it
how: A ul.agent-plan with data-state done, current or skipped on each item and aria-current="step" on the current one, a progress bar above it with the count. The queue and the todo list are lists the reader works through, each item's actions shown on hover and focus.
avoid: Marking the current step by its colour alone, without aria-current.

goal: Let the user ask an assistant a question and read its answer
how: The chat's thread, with the reader's messages in bubbles and the agent's turn as prose on the ground: its reasoning, its steps, the answer, its sources and what to do next. The prompt under it is one rounded field with its tools below the text.
avoid: Putting a long answer in a bubble, where four paragraphs and a code block read as a wall.

goal: Let the user see which sources an answer came from
how: A numbered .citation button inline in the answer opens its source in a popover with no script, and .citation-sources lists the same sources under the answer as source cards whose numbers match.
avoid: A citation named only by its digit, which a screen reader reads as a number.

goal: Let the user copy, rate or regenerate an answer
how: A .chat-feedback row under the answer: copy, regenerate, a rating with aria-pressed, and .chat-versions to page between the answers regenerated.
avoid: Replacing the earlier answer on regenerate, which leaves the reader no way back to the one they preferred.

goal: Let the user write a prompt and send, stop or retry it
how: .chat-composer--prompt draws the composer as one rounded field: the text on top, the tools under it — a menu of what can be added, toggles as chips, the model — and the submit button at the end, which shows send, stop or retry from data-state.
avoid: Three separate buttons for send, stop and retry: one button whose words follow the state keeps its place and its focus.

goal: Let the user choose which model answers
how: A button naming the model in use opens a flush popover holding an inline combo: a search over the models grouped by where they run, each with its provider's icon, a note and its shortcut.
avoid: A trigger that does not name the model in use, so the reader has to open it to find out.

goal: Let the user accept a suggested ending to what they are typing
how: The textarea and an empty .ghost-text in a .ghost-field, the suggestion in the textarea's data-suggestion; the rest shows after the caret, Tab writes it into the value and Escape dismisses it.
avoid: Not saying that Tab accepts: the ghost is not read out, so a hint the field names has to say it.

goal: Let the user act on the words they select in an answer
how: data-selection-toolbar on the thread names a .selection-toolbar the app wrote; the script opens it above the selection and fires sedna-selection with the action, the text and the message it came from.
avoid: Leaving the keyboard out: say where the reader will find it that Alt+F10 moves into the toolbar.

goal: Let the user go back to an earlier point in the conversation
how: A labelled divider across the thread with a bookmark icon, the time and a button that restores the conversation and its changes to there.
avoid: A restore with no time beside it, which leaves the reader guessing how much will be undone.

goal: Let the user keep an assistant open beside the page while they work
how: .drawer--dock on a modeless drawer that is a direct child of .layout: from 900px it is a column of the frame and the content narrows instead of being covered. A .chat-pane after its header holds the thread and the composer.
avoid: A modal drawer for the assistant, which makes the page it is meant to help with inert.

goal: Let the user read what the agent generated beside the conversation
how: An .artifact with its title, what it is, and its actions — versions, copy, download, open — in its head, as the aside of a split beside the conversation, or alone in a modeless drawer.
avoid: Pasting the generated file into the thread, where it scrolls away as the conversation about it goes on.

goal: Let the user talk to an agent by voice
how: A .voice-session with one thing on its stage, who is speaking, a live caption, the bars and the controls; the app writes --level once on the session and everything that shows the voice moves with it. The mic button's name says what pressing it does next.
avoid: Captions that are not live regions, so what the agent says never reaches a reader who cannot hear it.

goal: Let the user choose the microphone and the agent's voice
how: A select of the microphones the browser lists, and the voices as radios in a list, each with a button that plays a sample without choosing it.
avoid: An empty device list with no word about why: the browser lists nothing until the reader allows the microphone.
